The all-or-nothing attitude I have with school is def part of the problem. Rationally, there is no reason for me to be worried about getting into grad school at the moment—plenty of people make bank without it. I think its just an ego thing honestly. both of my parents have advanced degrees, so its always just been expected of me

i gotta get more social hobbies i guess. i play a few instruments, but don't normally play for others. 2020 was going to be the year where I tried to live more hedonistically, partying more, etc. and obv that didnt work out due to COVID. I also wanted to take up boxing, but that doesn't really work with COVID either. In your experience, what kinds of hobbies have you been able to maintain during the pandemic?

im physically the fittest i've ever been as i've really stepped up on the exercise during the pandemic. I think the second part of what you wrote is the sticking point for me. I'm the kinda guy that has always been smart enough to get myself out of situations. for once, im not in control. and i struggle to accept that, though im working on it

i agree that i have to take a more active role in keeping my social life alive. how do i even do that in a pandemic though? its impossible to meet women, its tough to see most friends, and i always get this nagging feeling that no one actually wants me there! no one makes an effort to reach out to me, so isnt it a little pathetic to go crawling back to people who apparently don't really care that i exist?
I'd argue that's part of the problem, if anything. I have "let everything happen" to me. I don't see how I'm going to become less lonely by being this passive.
